statement: The polynomial $p(x)=x^{3}-3x^{2}+ax+b$ has a factor $x-1$ and leaves remainder $5$ when divided by $x-2$. Find the values of $a$ and $b$, and hence find all three roots of $p(x)=0$.
solution: From $p(1)=0$ we get $1-3+a+b=0$, so $a+b=2$. From $p(2)=5$ we get $8-12+2a+b=5$, so $2a+b=9$. Subtracting gives $a=7$ and then $b=-5$. Thus $p(x)=x^{3}-3x^{2}+7x-5=(x-1)(x^{2}-2x+5)$, whose roots are $x=1$ and $x=1\pm2i$.
hints: Use $p(1)=0$ and $p(2)=5$ to get two equations.
Factor out $(x-1)$ from the resulting cubic.
